<issue identifier="MM-483">
<title>Harness: only one of UrgencyBadge's four states is reachable — no fixture for warning, critical, or expired alerts</title>
<description>
Follow-up to <issue id="df0a3db6-561f-4b3d-b373-232b5703f147" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-482/harness-alert-active-scenario-ages-into-an-expired-recovery-window">MM-482</issue>, which fixed `alert-active` ageing into an expired recovery window. That fix exposed a coverage gap it deliberately left alone.

## Problem

`seedAlert` has exactly one caller in the whole harness — `scenarios.ts`'s `alert-active`, seeding `isoHoursAgo(2)`.

`AlertDetailScreen` renders `<UrgencyBadge {urgency} …>` from `getUrgency(deadline, countdown.now)`. With a 2-hour-old alert, 70 hours of the 72-hour PLC window remain, so `deadline.ts` classifies it `safe`. Its thresholds:

| state | remaining |
| -- | -- |
| `safe` | ≥ 24h |
| `warning` | < 24h |
| `critical` | < 4h |
| `expired` | ≤ 0 |

So **only** `safe` **is reachable from the harness**. `warning`, `critical`, and `expired` have no fixture at all.

Note this is not a regression from <issue id="df0a3db6-561f-4b3d-b373-232b5703f147" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-482/harness-alert-active-scenario-ages-into-an-expired-recovery-window">MM-482</issue> — before that fix the *only* reachable state was `expired`, and it was reachable by accident (the fixture had decayed past its own deadline) rather than by design. Either way, three of the four states have never been reachable deliberately.

## Why it matters

These are exactly the states the design brief cares most about, and the ones hardest to reason about without seeing them:

* `critical` is the red, "act now" register — the visual peak of the whole alarm design.
* `expired` is the ashen "the moment to act has passed" state, and the only one where `AlertDetailScreen` disables the override button and relabels it "Recovery window expired". That disabled branch is currently unexercisable by hand.
* The badge's `safe` and the panel's `safe` deliberately mean different things (see `identity-status.ts`) — a divergence that is much easier to review with both a `safe` and a `critical` alert side by side.

`tools/screenshots/` already documents rare states (`rareState: true` shots), so these would also make the docs' alarm imagery cover more than the calmest case.

## Proposal

Add alert fixtures covering the missing states — for example `isoHoursAgo(60)` → ~12h remaining (`warning`), `isoHoursAgo(69)` → ~3h remaining (`critical`), and `isoHoursAgo(73)` → past the window (`expired`, which also reaches the disabled-override branch).

Open question worth deciding first: separate named scenarios (`alert-critical`, `alert-expired`, …) versus one scenario seeding several identities at different ages. The latter covers every state in a single screenshot and exercises the home list's multi-alert strip, but makes each individual state slower to reach when driving the harness by hand.

Whatever shape is chosen, extend `scenarios.test.ts`'s guard so each fixture asserts the urgency it is *supposed* to produce, rather than only that an alert exists — that weaker assertion is precisely what let <issue id="df0a3db6-561f-4b3d-b373-232b5703f147" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-482/harness-alert-active-scenario-ages-into-an-expired-recovery-window">MM-482</issue> rot undetected.

## Now cheaper than it used to be

Adding harness scenarios no longer drags a changelog fragment along: <issue id="df0a3db6-561f-4b3d-b373-232b5703f147" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-482/harness-alert-active-scenario-ages-into-an-expired-recovery-window">MM-482</issue> exempted `apps/*/src/lib/harness/` from the changelog gate, so this is a pure test-tooling change.
</description>

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Two different "urgency" vocabularies coexist: `getUrgency(deadline)` (what the **badge** shows — how much of the 72h PLC window is left) and `deriveIdentityPanelState()` (what the **panel** shows — any live alert is `critical` regardless of time left). The existing test asserts the panel's, which is why it can pass while three badge states stay unreachable.
- `seedAlert(seed, createdAt)` derives the alert's `cid` from the seed alone, so any multi-alert fixture needs distinct seeds or the fake will emit colliding CIDs.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

options.label: Separate named scenarios (Recommended)
options.description: Add `alert-warning`, `alert-critical`, `alert-expired` alongside `alert-active` (safe). Each is one tap to reach by hand and one shot per state for docs; costs three new ScenarioName entries and three AGENTS.md/docs mentions.

options.label: One multi-age scenario
options.description: A single `alert-spectrum` seeding four identities at 2h/60h/69h/73h. Covers every state in one screenshot and exercises the home list's multi-alert strip, but reaching a specific state by hand means navigating into the right identity.

options.label: Both
options.description: Three named single-state scenarios plus a spectrum scenario for the multi-alert strip. Maximum coverage, largest surface to keep in sync.

content.text:
MM-483 done and committed on `claude/urgencybadge-state-fixtures-ebb47f`.

**What changed**
- [scenarios.ts](apps/identity-wallet/src/lib/harness/scenarios.ts) — added `alert-warning` (~12h left), `alert-critical` (~3h left), `alert-expired` (past the window). All four alert presets now share one `alertScenario(hoursAgo)` builder, since the age *is* the fixture.
- [scenarios.test.ts](apps/identity-wallet/src/lib/harness/scenarios.test.ts) — replaced the "an alert exists" assertion with a table asserting the badge urgency each fixture must produce (`getUrgency(getDeadline(createdAt))`, the way `AlertDetailScreen` measures it), plus the panel urgency, plus a guard that no alert preset can ever fold to the panel's `safe`.
- [AGENTS.md](apps/identity-wallet/AGENTS.md) — preset list updated.

**Verification**
- Full wallet suite: 229 passed (26 files); `svelte-check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Mutation-checked the new guard — reverting `alert-critical` to a 2h age fails it (`expected 'safe' to be 'critical'`), so it bites on exactly the decay that let MM-482 rot.
- Drove the browser harness and confirmed each state renders: `critical` → red "2h 59m remaining", override enabled; `warning` → "11h 59m remaining"; `expired` → ashen "Expired" with the override **disabled and relabelled "Recovery window expired"** — the branch the issue called unexercisable by hand.
- No changelog fragment needed: `changelog-check.sh` exempts both `apps/*/src/lib/harness/` and `AGENTS.md`.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The old guard's weakness was structural, not an oversight: `alerts.length > 0` is invariant under time, while everything the fixture exists to demonstrate is a function of `Date.now()`. Assertions on live-clock fixtures have to name the derived property, not the raw data.
- `alert-active` and `alert-critical` produce *different* badge states but the *same* panel state — that's `identity-status.ts` deliberately refusing to let remaining time soften an active intrusion. Having both fixtures makes that divergence reviewable side by side rather than a comment.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

I stopped at the commit — say the word and I'll push and open the PR (which also moves MM-483 to In Review). I left `tools/screenshots/` alone; adding `rareState: true` shots for these is a natural follow-up if you want the docs imagery to cover the alarm states.
